title: Brent's 12% surge pushes Asian PFY Higher by up to 2.61%
summary:
PFY prices strengthened in Asia in the week ended July 24, with TexPro showing Chinese grades up 1.33-2.61 per cent and India's benchmark up 2.29 per cent.
The move was driven by a more than 12 per cent Brent crude rise, lifting naphtha, PTA, MEG and PET costs.
Pakistan's flat DTY and POY benchmarks signal weak mill demand, not stability, complicating sourcing decisions.

title: ICE cotton closes higher on weaker dollar, technical buying
summary:
ICE cotton futures rose for a fifth straight session, with the December 2026 contract settling 0.90 cent higher at 80.88 cents per pound as a weaker US dollar, technical buying and strong Chinese reserve purchases supported prices.
Tight certified stocks also aided sentiment, while traders now await the US Federal Reserve, weather and export demand for further direction.

title: Asia's regenerated MMCF complex holds firm across the value chain
summary:
TexPro benchmarks for Asia’s specialty MMCF complex were unchanged in the week of July 20–24, with Modal fibre flat in China, India and Pakistan.
Modal, Liva Eco, Ecovero and Tencel yarn prices in 30/1 and 40/1 counts showed no week-on-week movement across the TexPro panel.
Stable contracts aid third-quarter sourcing plans, but tariffs, pulp and Pakistan energy costs remain watch points.

title: Germany’s Groz-Beckert to unveil textile innovations at CINTE 2026
summary:
Groz-Beckert will showcase advanced nonwovens and knitting technologies at CINTE Techtextil China 2026, highlighting greater precision, efficiency and machine reliability.
New felting needles, carding solutions and expanded warp knitting modules aim to simplify production while improving performance across textile manufacturing processes.

title: Austria’s Lenzing shifts focus to nonwovens, resets textiles strategy
summary:
Lenzing is accelerating its transformation by prioritising higher-margin nonwovens while reducing exposure to commodity textile fibres.
The strategy includes production consolidation, workforce reductions, €120 million (~$136.8 million) in savings and refinancing to strengthen profitability.
The company targets a 20–25 per cent EBITDA margin over the medium term.

title: Italian textile machinery orders rebound 25% in Q2 2026
summary:

summary:

Farmer incentives, hybrid varieties, more acreage and credit support are central to delivery.

summary:

summary:
